reasons: No tests are visible in this packet.
The copying step depends on validation running again, which the code comments discuss; that behaviour is not tested here.

terms.meaning: An input that the benefit depends on and that is varied in the sensitivity test.
The gap between the net benefit at the low end and at the high end of a driver.
A range of values with a low, base and high figure.
A check that data has the right shape and values before use.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and list of drivers
sections.what: Explains the one-at-a-time approach and lists the five inputs that are varied: baseline effort, automatable share, assisted share, assisted efficiency gain and adoption ramp.
sections.why: The docstring says a joint worst case is not believed by readers, so the one-at-a-time approach is used.
sections.watch_out: Adding a driver here makes it appear in the report. It must actually change the benefit, or it will always show zero.

sections.name: _collapsed
sections.title: Collapsing a range to one end
sections.what: Turns a range into a single value by setting its low, base and high to the same end value, keeping the same kind of range.
sections.why: Used to fix one driver at one end of its range while the rest stay as they are.
sections.watch_out: If a value that is not a range is passed in, this will fail.

sections.name: _pinned
sections.title: Copying records with one driver fixed
sections.what: Makes a copy of every record with one driver pinned at one end, then checks the copy is valid.
sections.why: The comments say copying alone skips validation, so the copy is validated again. The comments also say the check cannot fail for the current drivers.
sections.watch_out: A validation error on a copy would stop the whole sensitivity run.

sections.name: sensitivities
sections.title: Ranking the drivers
sections.what: For each driver, works out the net benefit at its low and high ends for each currency, records the gap, and sorts the results with the largest gap first within each currency.
sections.why: Ranking lets a reader check the most influential assumption first.
sections.watch_out: A currency missing from one of the two runs is shown as zero, which can hide a real result.

summary: Moves each key assumption to its low and high end, one at a time, and ranks them by how much each one changes the net benefit.
purpose: Shows which assumption a reader should check first. The ranking tells the reader where the answer is most sensitive.
why: The docstring says moving every assumption together gives a worst case nobody believes. Moving one at a time answers which assumption matters most.
how: Step 1: for each driver, make two copies of the inputs, one with the driver fixed at its low end and one at its high end, with all other inputs unchanged. Step 2: recalculate the net benefit for each copy, per currency. Step 3: record the net at low, the net at high and the gap between them. Step 4: sort so the largest gap comes first within each currency.
inputs: The full set of engine inputs and a function that returns net benefit per currency.
outputs: A list of sensitivity results, one per driver per currency, sorted by currency and then by size of gap.
risks: A driver that has no effect shows a gap of zero, which trains readers to skip the table. A currency missing from one run is treated as zero, which can look like a real zero result.
debug: If a driver always shows zero, check that the driver is actually used by the benefit calculation. If the ranking looks odd, compare the low and high net values for that driver. If a copy fails validation, check the most recent change to the value parameters.
